ranked_angles.angle: External unsat-core selection plus small kernel-replayed arithmetic proofs
ranked_angles.new_relative_to_existing: bv_omega_g normalizes only the goal; it cannot select necessary hypotheses. KNormCache caches simplification but does not remove irrelevant arithmetic assumptions. A Z3 core can identify the necessary premises, after which Lean omega/bv reasoning proves the original goal from those premises.
ranked_angles.robustness_test: Rename/reorder hypotheses, add 0/8/16 irrelevant subtraction-chain facts, and remove the sole necessary bound. Report solved/failed obligations and diagnostic quality; final proof is always kernel-checked.
ranked_angles.success_metric: Stable results and bounded replay work under context growth; smaller proof dependencies; end-to-end elaboration includes solver IPC and replay.

ranked_angles.angle: Typed BV/Nat word-level planning instead of flattening all machine facts into modular integer arithmetic
ranked_angles.new_relative_to_existing: Existing bv_decide and bv_omega are already used. The missing planning layer chooses which terms stay bitvectors, which get bounded Nat views, and which shared carries/wrap conditions need proofs. It should emit a small sequence of existing bridge lemmas plus sliced arithmetic, rather than reify an entire symbolic machine state.
ranked_angles.robustness_test: Equivalent arithmetic reassociation, 32/64-bit width changes, positive/zero/saturating-subtraction boundaries, and rejection of missing no-wrap/sign bounds.
ranked_angles.success_metric: One clear typed certificate per arithmetic intent; preserve exact theorem statements and audit added axioms; measure solver+replay rather than solver time alone.

ranked_angles.angle: SMT-style read-over-write normal forms over finite maps and indexed sequence views
ranked_angles.new_relative_to_existing: Archived Sequence/SequenceShapes already offer index search and shared splice templates, and FsAbsDelta already supplies operation-specific delta laws. New work should generate an observation-level store/select certificate and necessary key/index cases across maps AND views, while keeping implementations opaque. It must not merely rerun unrestricted grind or restore a template library.
ranked_angles.robustness_test: Reorder independent updates, insert overwritten writes, rename keys, vary clipping bounds, and reject missing key disequalities or out-of-range list observations.
ranked_angles.success_metric: Proofs state update semantics and footprint, with generated pointwise cases; kernel replay must reuse established lookup/length laws. Ghost authority and crash protocol remain explicit.

ranked_angles.angle: Resource-routing planner with explicit fraction, extent, and restoration constraints
ranked_angles.new_relative_to_existing: BigSep accessors, FrameFilter, LayoutResources, and archived typed Access certificates already perform individual splitting/composition. New capability would infer a valid sequence of existing spatial rules from desired read/write windows, preserving linear restoration continuations and fraction constraints, and explain impossible overlap/width requests.
ranked_angles.robustness_test: Alter padding, source fraction, slice nesting, ownership order and alias constraints; solver must reject full-write requests backed only by fractional ownership.
ranked_angles.success_metric: User supplies access intent and real domain invariant; planner derives a replayable route. Do not ask external arithmetic to invent ghost resources or justify invariant opening.

ranked_angles.angle: Shared symbolic DAG certificates and cutpoint obligation diagnostics
ranked_angles.new_relative_to_existing: KNormCache already caches within declarations; uwk_run +merge already merges equal-state branches; the current whole-function backend already decodes and symbolically computes blocks. The next distinction is sharing parameterized proofs across blocks/declarations and surfacing only unsolved invariant/resource obligations, rather than rebuilding a second interpreter.
ranked_angles.robustness_test: Equivalent register allocation and branch refactoring regenerate a certificate without changing domain invariants; wrong targets and insufficient call contracts yield focused failures.
ranked_angles.success_metric: Fewer brittle intermediate-state annotations; predictable diagnostics; separately measure certificate regeneration, shared helper check, and cached consumer check.

findings: General kernel reduction of SAT certificates approached 3.3 GiB on tiny examples; direct bit proofs were cheaper. Do not indiscriminately bit-blast all VCs.
Restricted per-client sequence grind made five focused module medians sum 28.447 -> 34.173 seconds; reduced source was not faster checking.
Shared sequence certificates improved incremental checks versus per-client search (35.671 -> 27.041 seconds), but the 8.359-second helper erased first-pass savings.
Unfolding overwrite exhausted grind case-split limits; lookup/length observations made the same theorem succeed. Preserve opaque data-structure representations.
Typed resource access certificates passed six integrations but aggregate median improvement was only 2.8% before helper cost; algebra alone is not an automatic planner.
CPU pin equality closure survived renaming/reordering/reversal and inserted hops; already explored and not a new primary target.
Early benchmark rounds did not explicitly pass -j1; only later sequence/access rounds enforced one Lean worker. Historical measurements are not new results.

current_negative_evidence.finding: Restricted grind field lookup increased a paired module median from 2.542 to 4.545 seconds; deterministic routing retained.
Exact ownState cannot coexist with production resourceInv under stateInterp. Pure external certificates need the footprint/resource boundary, not extra exact-state ownership.
Current branch equality debugging found global simp recursion; restricted simp only plus kernel_rfl succeeded. New solvers should publish narrow observation/replay interfaces.
